Definition: Percentage of the national population covered by at least one 4G/LTE mobile network signal, whether or not they subscribe to the service. 4G is the practical minimum for meaningful broadband connectivity enabling digital services.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Ethio Telecom's FY2024/25 results (reported by TechAfrica News and Extensia, Aug 2025) show 4G population coverage rising from 37.5% to 70.8%, which falls in the 50-74% band, not 75-89%; ITU DataHub gives a lower 44% for 2024. The original source (a Huawei collaboration article) does not actually state 71%. Revised to 3; flagged for human review given the gap between operator self-reported and ITU figures.

Definition: Affordability of mobile broadband data, measured as the cost of a basic mobile data plan (1-2GB) as a percentage of GNI per capita. The UN Broadband Commission target is below 2% of monthly GNI per capita. Affordability is the single largest barrier to internet adoption in Africa.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: ITU's Digital Development Dashboard (the same source cited originally) reports the mobile broadband basket at 3.4% of GNI per capita (2022), which falls in the Moderate (2-5%) band, not Affordable (1-2%). Original code contradicted its own cited evidence; revised to 3.

Definition: Percentage of individuals who used the internet (from any location, via any device) in the last three months. This measures actual internet adoption beyond network availability, capturing the combined effect of infrastructure, affordability, digital literacy, and relevance.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: World Bank (June 2025) reports internet penetration at 19% in 2024; DataReportal's Digital 2026 report gives 21.7% at end of 2025. Both fall in the 15-29% band, not 30-49% — even the figure the original comment cited (21.3%) is itself in the 15-29% band, so it was miscoded. Revised to 2.

Definition: The country's total international internet bandwidth capacity per internet user, indicating the quality and capacity of the country's connection to the global internet. Determined by submarine cable landings (for coastal states), cross-border terrestrial fibre (for landlocked states), and satellite links.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The same ITU source cited originally states international bandwidth per internet user of 22 kbit/s (2022), which falls in the 20-49 kbit/s (Moderate) band, not 5-19 kbit/s. No more recent ITU figure was found. Revised to 3.

Definition: Whether the country has an operational Internet Exchange Point (IXP) and its maturity. IXPs enable local internet traffic to be exchanged domestically rather than being routed internationally, reducing latency, costs, and dependence on foreign infrastructure. Critical for local digital ecosystem development.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed via Internet Society Pulse and PeeringDB (updated 2026): Addix in Addis Ababa remains Ethiopia's only IXP, with 3 members and 21 Gbps capacity, operating as a sandboxed IXP under ECA supervision. Matches 'Single IXP with limited participation'; code unchanged, corroborated with a second source.

Definition: Unique mobile subscriber penetration rate as a percentage of the total population. Measures the proportion of individuals who subscribe to a mobile service (not SIM cards, which can be multiple per person). Mobile phones are the primary device for internet access in Africa.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The variable requires unique subscriber penetration, not SIM/connections. World Bank (June 2025) reports unique mobile subscriber penetration rose from 26% (2020) to 33% (2024) — far below the 68.4% 'connections' figure the original code was based on, which measures SIM/cellular connections rather than unique subscribers. Revised to 2; flagged for human review given the large gap between connection-based and subscriber-based estimates and reliance on a single (albeit authoritative) source.

Definition: Percentage of mobile connections using smartphones (as opposed to feature phones or basic phones). Smartphones are the minimum device requirement for accessing most digital public infrastructure services, apps, and mobile internet.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The original comment's '97.6% broadband' figure actually refers to the share of mobile connections that are 3G/4G/5G (per DataReportal), not smartphone device adoption — it does not support the assigned code. Birr Metrics (Oct 2025) reports high device costs and limited supply are constraining smartphone uptake. No precise, current Ethiopia-specific smartphone % was found. Revised to a cautious 3 (40-59%) as an estimate; flagged for human review to confirm against GSMA Intelligence country data.

Definition: The availability and presence of major cloud service providers (hyperscale and regional) operating in or serving the country with local or near-local infrastructure. Cloud availability determines access to scalable computing resources for government, business, and startups.
Value Name: Served remotely from distant regions only (>100ms latency)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The originally cited article discusses GCP's Johannesburg region and does not mention Ethiopia at all — an unrelated source. Fresh evidence shows Wingu Africa (a regional East African cloud/data-centre operator) has launched a local private-cloud platform (WCX) in Ethiopia, interoperable with Azure/AWS, and Raxio's Addis Ababa data centre offers on-site access to public/private/hybrid cloud providers. No hyperscaler (AWS/Azure/GCP) has a confirmed region or edge node in Ethiopia itself; the nearest hyperscale regions remain in South Africa. Revised to 4 ('at least one provider with local presence'); flagged for human review as Wingu's Ethiopia launch is very recent and its 'major provider' status is judgement-dependent.

Definition: The country's overall cybersecurity preparedness, based on the ITU Global Cybersecurity Index (GCI). Covers legal measures, technical measures, organisational measures, capacity development, and cooperation. Essential for trust in stored data and digital services.

revision_notes: Confirmed: ITU's Global Cybersecurity Index 2024 gives Ethiopia a score of 76.34 (Tier 3, 'Establishing'), corroborated by PKF Ethiopia's analysis of the same report. Falls within the 60-79 (Advancing) band; code unchanged. Source upgraded from a LinkedIn post to the ITU report itself plus the same advisory analysis via its own site.

Definition: Whether the country has enacted legal or regulatory requirements mandating that certain categories of data (personal data, government data, financial data, or critical infrastructure data) be stored within national borders. Central to data sovereignty debates in Africa.
Value Name: Comprehensive requirements for personal data or broad categories
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed via the Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024 text (Article 31, 'Data Sovereignty'): all locally collected personal data must be stored on servers in Ethiopia, with additional controls on 'critical' personal data and prior approval required for cross-border transfer of sensitive data. Matches 'Comprehensive requirements for personal data'; code unchanged, source upgraded to the primary legal text.

redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed: World Bank WDI reports 55.4% electricity access for Ethiopia in 2023 (latest available), consistent with the original 55% figure and the 50-74% band. Code unchanged; source refreshed to World Bank/Trading Economics.

Definition: Whether the country has established policies, regulations, and programmes supporting off-grid and distributed energy solutions (mini-grids, solar home systems). These are critical for extending ICT infrastructure to unserved areas beyond the central grid.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Ethiopia has a comprehensive policy framework (National Electrification Programme 2.0, targeting a 65% grid/35% off-grid split), but actual deployment lags well behind plan: only 13 mini-grids were installed by December 2024 (EU/EnDev), and the World Bank's $500m ADELE project has been restructured due to cost overruns, with its mini-grid component scaled back. This better matches 'active policy with some deployment' than 'comprehensive framework with significant deployment'. Revised to 3.

Definition: The maturity of the country's technology startup ecosystem, based on the number of tech startups, venture capital activity, accelerators/incubators, and the presence of a supportive ecosystem. Africa's startup scene is well-documented by trackers like Partech, Disrupt Africa, and Briter Bridges.
Value Name: Developing (growing startup base, regular funding rounds, several hubs)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: More recent evidence (2023-2025) shows a growing base of funded startups beyond the single 2020 example cited — Kubik ($3.34m in 2023, further $1.9-5.2m in 2024) and Better Auth ($5m in 2025, backed by Y Combinator and Sequoia India) — alongside several active hubs (see Technology and Innovation Hubs row). Supports 'Developing (growing startup base, regular funding rounds, several hubs)'; code confirmed unchanged, sources refreshed and diversified.

Definition: The number and activity level of technology hubs, incubators, accelerators, and co-working spaces focused on technology and innovation. These provide physical infrastructure and support for tech entrepreneurship and skills development.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: AfriLabs' Ethiopia country page lists at least 4 network-affiliated hubs (xHub, Startup Factory Ethiopia, blueMoon, Iceaddis); a 2026 roundup identifies around 10 active hubs/coworking spaces nationally, including outside Addis Ababa (e.g. Jigjiga, Hawassa). This sits close to the boundary between '3-9 hubs' and '10-24 hubs'. The original source (a Facebook post) was too weak to verify. Kept at 3 as the more conservative reading; flagged for human review given the evidence sits near the band boundary.

Definition: The size and vibrancy of the local software developer and technology professional community. Measured through proxies such as GitHub activity, Stack Overflow representation, local tech meetup groups, and developer surveys. Indicates the country's capacity to build and maintain digital systems locally.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: GitHub's Octoverse 2023 report (authoritative primary source) states Ethiopia had over 94,000 developers on GitHub in 2023, with 32% year-on-year growth — well above the 50,000+ threshold for the 'Mature' band. The original code (3, 1,000-10,000) was based on a vaguer 2022 characterisation and substantially understates the current evidence. Revised to 5.

Definition: The gap between men and women in mobile internet usage or internet access. Based on the GSMA Mobile Gender Gap data or ITU gender-disaggregated ICT statistics. A smaller gap indicates more equitable access to digital opportunities.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The original comment's '81% rural gap' is a sub-population figure (rural women vs. others) from a GSMA blog post, not the national mobile internet gender gap the variable asks for, so it does not actually support the assigned code. GSMA's Mobile Gender Gap Report 2024 gives a Sub-Saharan Africa regional gender gap of 32% (2023) but does not include full Ethiopia survey data (Ethiopia's sample was disrupted by conflict in 2022-23); country figures in the same report (men 79% vs women 57% mobile ownership) imply a gap broadly in that range. Kept at 2 as a plausible regional-proxy estimate but flagged for human review given the lack of robust Ethiopia-specific GSMA survey data.
